nodes.summary: If `P` is a finite generating family, each ball `{g | |g|_P ≤ n}` is finite: it is the image of the finite set of words of length at most `n`.
nodes.title: Word balls of a finite generating family are finite

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the value of the growth function of $P$ at $n$ is at most the order of $G$, since every ball is a subset of $G$.
nodes.title: The growth function is bounded by the order of the group

nodes.summary: If `P` is a finite generating family and the balls of `Q` are finite, there is `K : ℕ` with `γ_P(n) ≤ γ_Q(K n)` for every `n`.
nodes.title: Growth functions of two generating families dominate each other

nodes.summary: If a generating family $P$ of a group $G$ has polynomial growth, then the growth function of $P$ is positive at every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth makes the growth function positive

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the growth function of $P$ is positive at $n$: the ball of radius $n$ contains the identity.
nodes.title: The growth function of a finite group is positive

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a group $G$, the growth function of $P$ takes the value $1$ at $0$: the ball of radius $0$ consists of the identity element alone.
nodes.title: The growth function at radius zero

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$. The growth function $\gamma_P$ of $P$ assigns to each natural number $n$ the number of elements $g \in G$ whose word length with respect to $P$ is at most $n$, that is, the cardinality of the ball of radius $n$ in the word metric of $P$; when this ball is infinite, $\gamma_P(n)$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Growth function of a generating family

nodes.summary: For two finite generating families $P$ and $Q$ of a group $G$, $P$ has polynomial growth if and only if $Q$ does. Polynomial growth is therefore a property of the finitely generated group: Gromov's remark that "this definition does not depend on the particular choice of the generators and so this notion is correctly defined for the finitely generated groups".
nodes.title: Polynomial growth is independent of the finite generating set

nodes.summary: The ball of radius `n` of `Multiplicative ℤ` for the generator `ofAdd 1` is finite with at most `2 (n + 1)` elements (it has exactly `2n + 1`), so `intGenerators` has polynomial growth of degree `1`.
nodes.title: The infinite cyclic group has polynomial growth

nodes.summary: Every generating family of a finite group has polynomial growth: its growth function is bounded by the order of the group, a polynomial of degree $0$.
nodes.title: Finite groups have polynomial growth

nodes.summary: If a group $G$ has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index, then every finite generating family of $G$ has polynomial growth. This is due to Wolf, Bass and Guivarc'h; Gromov recalls it in the introduction of his paper (his reference [14] and Tits's appendix) as the converse of his theorem.
nodes.title: Virtually nilpotent groups have polynomial growth

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$, with growth function $\gamma_P$. Then $P$ has polynomial growth if, for every natural number $n$, the ball of radius $n$ (the set of elements of $G$ of word length at most $n$ with respect to $P$) is finite, and there are natural numbers $C$ and $d$ such that $\gamma_P(n) \le C (n + 1)^d$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth

nodes.summary: If some generating family `Q` of `G` has polynomial growth, then every finite generating family `P` has polynomial growth (Gromov, *Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps*, Publ. Math. IHÉS 53 (1981), p. 54).
nodes.title: Polynomial growth transfers between generating families

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite generating families of groups $G$ and $H$, and let $f : G \to H$ be a quasi-isometric embedding for the left-invariant word metrics: $|g^{-1} g'|_P \le L\, |f(g)^{-1} f(g')|_Q + C$ and $|f(g)^{-1} f(g')|_Q \le L\, |g^{-1} g'|_P + C$ for all $g, g'$. If $Q$ has polynomial growth, so does $P$. The map $f$ need not be a homomorphism, injective, or coarsely surjective.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth is a quasi-isometry invariant

nodes.summary: If a group $G$ has a finite generating family $P$ of polynomial growth, then $G$ has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
nodes.title: Gromov's polynomial growth theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
